title: Sightline rubric pack
description: A rubric pack is the lens Sightline reports a course review through. It carries the instrument's own rows and identifiers, the rating bands printed on that instrument, and zero or more bindings from each row to a capability tag. A pack with no bindings at all is valid and usable: its rows route to the extraction layer. Nothing here requires a pack to be an OSCQR derivative, to carry an OPEN SUNY number, or to be crosswalked to any other instrument.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the pack was written against.

id.description: Stable identifier for the pack. Chosen once and never renumbered, so a revised import diffs against it.

name.description: What to call this instrument in the interface and the report.

version.description: The instrument's own version, as a string because instruments are numbered like '3.1.3'. Free text; Sightline does not order it.

source.description: Where the rows came from, so a re-import of a revised instrument can be told apart from a hand edit.

title.description: The instrument's own title as printed on it.

workbook.description: Filename of the workbook imported, without a directory. A path is not recorded: it can name a person's home directory.

key_source.description: What the row codes were built from. 'positional_index' is a warning in itself: an instrument with no stable identifier of its own renumbers when a row is inserted, and a re-import cannot diff cleanly (SPEC §11).

notes.description: Anything the importer had to decide, stated so a reviewer can check it.

priority_order.description: The instrument's own priority labels, most important first. Action-plan ordering uses this. A row with no priority sorts after every labelled one, which is what the mobile block of the reference instrument needs.

rating_scale.description: The rating names and the effort bands PRINTED ON THIS INSTRUMENT. Band thresholds are pack data because they belong to the instrument; the per-defect costs that get summed into them are global configuration, calibrated once (SPEC §07).

sufficiently_present.description: What this instrument calls 'a detector ran and found nothing'. It has no band, because it is 'no qualifying defects found' rather than zero hours.

no_response.description: The default cell state. Every Tier C row stays here and so does every row Sightline could not establish.

bands.description: Effort bands in ascending order. The last one is open-ended and carries a null ceiling.

rating.description: Sightline's internal name for the band. Distinct from the label so two instruments with different wording share one effort model.

label.description: What this instrument prints for the band.

up_to_hours.description: Inclusive upper bound in hours; null on the last band, which is open-ended.

range_label.description: The range as printed on the instrument, e.g. '1/2 hour or less'. Quoted rather than derived, so the report can show the instrument's own words.

sections.description: The instrument's own sections, declared so the report can be grouped in instrument order and so an optional block can be switched off.

code.description: Short code for the section, used by criteria to point at it.

optional.description: Whether this section may be switched off without invalidating the pack. THIS IS THE OPTIONAL-RENDER FLAG: a block that only applies to some courses — a mobile-standards section, say — declares itself optional here, and only a section that has done so may set 'enabled' to false.

enabled.description: Whether this pack switches the section on. Defaults true. Setting it false requires 'optional': true, so a mandatory block can never be dropped by a typo.

note.description: Why the section is optional, or why it is switched off. Rendered beside the omission so a gap is stated rather than silent.

criteria.description: The rows. At least one: an instrument with no rows is an import that failed, not an empty instrument.

code.description: The row's identifier, and the key EVERY lookup uses. Never a positional index into this array: the reference instrument skips an index inside one of its categories, and index-walking silently misaligns criteria.

section.description: The code of a section declared above.

text.description: The criterion as written on the instrument, verbatim.

tier.description: Determinacy tier (SPEC §02). A: computed by a parser. B: located and quoted. C: pedagogical judgement, never pre-rated. D: not determinable from course artifacts.

priority.description: The instrument's own priority label, or null. NULLABLE ON PURPOSE — the reference instrument's mobile block carries no flag at all, and ordering must tolerate that rather than inventing one.

bindings.description: Capability tags this row is about. ZERO IS NORMAL and is the ordinary steady state for a freshly imported third-party instrument: the row carries NO_DETERMINISTIC_COVERAGE and routes to the extraction layer. Tags are course-quality concepts from sightline/capabilities.yaml, never detector ids. A tag this build does not recognise is reported and the row degrades to no deterministic coverage — it does not invalidate the pack.

note.description: A statement carried into the report beside this row — what a Tier D row cannot be determined from, for instance.

source_ids.description: The identifiers the source instrument carries for this row, kept verbatim so a re-import diffs cleanly instead of silently renumbering criteria (SPEC §11). Free-form: a third-party instrument's identifiers are its own business, and nothing here requires an OPEN SUNY number or any other instrument's numbering.
